clue.text: Aim to wrap Eliza's present: superlative form of rum

indicators.note: to wrap means the aim's word goes around the other piece like paper round a gift

parts.note: an aim is a quest, something you seek
Eliza Doolittle in Pygmalion drops her aitches, so 'here' (present) comes out as 'ere

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to gift-wrap Eliza's birthday present, with a stray grammar note about the word rum.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza is Shaw's Cockney flower girl, whose dropped aitch turns 'here' into 'ERE. 'Rum' is old British slang for odd or strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is British slang for odd or peculiar, and its superlative, most peculiar, is this word.

clue.text: Ill-equipped to seal crack

indicators.note: the outer word seals the shorter word up inside its own letters

explanation.surface: A badly equipped workman tries to seal a crack in the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark or wisecrack, the same as a clever one-liner.

clue.text: Setter's measure and setter's award

parts.note: an em is a unit of width used by typesetters
the crossword setter's means 'my', the setter speaking of himself

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler boasts of both his tape measure and his prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Setter' is a typesetter, whose unit is the EM; the second is the crossword setter, whose 'setter's' becomes MY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the statuette awarded annually for excellence in American television.

clue.text: Artist sending away third and last journalist with new logo

indicators.note: the artist's name loses its third letter and its last letter, which are sent away

parts.note: Rembrandt, the Dutch master painter
ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A painter dismisses the third and final reporter, now that the paper has a new masthead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sending away third and last' removes M and T from REMBRANDT, leaving REBRAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that has been rebranded has been given a new corporate image, typically a new logo.

clue.text: Where ruthlessness ultimately left sides crushed?

definitions.text: Where ruthlessness ultimately left sides crushed?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of ruthlessness

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, so left sides are ports
crushed means ground, as coffee beans are ground

explanation.surface: A stadium where a merciless team flattened their opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a playing field is just the place where one side ruthlessly crushes the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Teams meet and are beaten on a playing field, the venue described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Jiffy bag containing one picture

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, informally a mo

indicators.note: the bag word contains the other piece inside it

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch in anatomy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A padded Jiffy envelope holds a single photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: Jiffy bag is a brand of padded envelope, but here 'Jiffy' means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made from small tiles or pieces of glass set together is this kind of artwork.

clue.text: Topless bathing suit Victorian perhaps?

indicators.note: a topless word loses its first letter

parts.note: cozzie is Australian and British slang for a swimming costume

explanation.surface: A question about whether a topless swimsuit is a Victorian garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' takes the C off COZZIE. 'Victorian' is not the 19th century but a person from the Australian state of Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the state of Victoria is an Australian, colloquially an Aussie, here spelt with zeds.

clue.text: English runs within reach after total scored briskly

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the total

parts.note: total means all

indicators.note: within means the runs letter sits inside the reach phrase

parts.note: to reach a place is to get to it
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket report: an English side piles up runs in pursuit of the total.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into GET TO after its G, giving GRETTO; ALL and E come first.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction marks a passage to be played fairly briskly, a little slower than allegro.

clue.text: Conservative Party member that's crazy TV talk show star, potentially?

parts.note: the Mad Hatter is a member of the tea party in Alice in Wonderland
the box is a colloquial name for television

explanation.surface: A Tory politician, said to be mad, becomes a television talk show host.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Party' is the Mad Hatter's tea party, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks incessantly might be just the right sort to host a talk show, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Young bride initially wears kimono specially for me

indicators.note: something worn goes around the wearer, so the kimono letters wrap the bride's
specially means the letters are arranged in a special new way
initially means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A young bride is wearing a kimono made especially for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' puts the bride's initials inside the kimono, the way a garment surrounds its wearer; 'specially' scrambles the kimono to INMOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this phrase means in my opinion, so it is a way of saying as far as I am concerned.

clue.text: Plant a field with maize regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field

explanation.surface: Advice to sow a field with maize at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of maize, AZ.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering shrub, related to the rhododendron, is a garden plant.

clue.text: Camera-gazing eccentric's religious air

indicators.note: eccentric means odd and out of the usual order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An odd person stares into the camera while singing a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous Christian hymn, and an air is a tune or song.

clue.text: He could get bang with tame shot

definitions.text: He could get bang with tame shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer might take a punch even from a feeble swing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a light boxer could take a bang, even from a tame shot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boxer of a light weight class, someone who takes a bang in the ring.

clue.text: Go on marathon walk, roping in the mater's new chap?

indicators.note: roping in means the outer phrase takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a marathon walk means you step far

explanation.surface: Mum's new partner goes on a long sponsored walk and recruits others.
explanation.walkthrough: THE goes into STEP FAR, between the A and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is old British slang for mother, and her new husband would be a step-parent to her children.

clue.text: Mole, one on the nose perhaps, cut into by fresh autopsy

indicators.note: cut into means the first piece is split open by the second

parts.note: a bet placed on the nose backs a horse to win

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are newly arranged

explanation.surface: A pathologist's fresh autopsy cuts into a mole on the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the nose' is a racing term for a wager to win; 'fresh' scrambles the post-mortem word into AUTYSPO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole on the face, natural or painted on, is often called this attractive mark.

clue.text: Material from tidy bed appearing on time

indicators.note: appearing on means one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: to weed a flower bed is to tidy it

explanation.surface: Fabric from a neatly made bed is laid out on time.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bed' is a flower bed, not one for sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: This rough woollen cloth is a fabric, so a kind of material.

clue.text: Reference body of correspondence in Spectator

indicators.note: in means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: a spectator is a gazer

indicators.note: the body of a word is all but its first and last letters

parts.note: a letter is a piece of correspondence

explanation.surface: A reference to a set of letters published in The Spectator magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'body of' strips the outer letters from LETTER, leaving ETTE. The Spectator is a British magazine, but here it is just a watcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A geographical dictionary is a reference book listing places.

clue.text: Draw energy, concealing age, even

indicators.note: concealing means the age word is hidden inside the others

parts.note: to draw someone in is to tempt them
an era is an age
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Drawing on one's energy while hiding one's age.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate climate or manner is moderate, steady and even.

clue.text: Note replacement hammer used by forge

parts.note: to pound something is to hammer it
to coin money is to mint or forge it

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's hammer is used at the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the one-pound note was withdrawn in 1988, replaced by a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The British coin worth one pound replaced the old paper note of the same value.

clue.text: Force men back underground

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force

indicators.note: back means the men's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, enlisted men

explanation.surface: The police force sends its officers back below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) reads backwards as RO.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground railway in a city, such as Paris's, is called this.

clue.text: Thus topless bathing suits may be seen round City!

definitions.text: Thus topless bathing suits may be seen round City!

indicators.note: round means the trimmed word goes around the city
topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: NY stands for New York City
something that goes with an outfit suits it

explanation.surface: In a permissive city, people walk around in topless swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a permissive scene, with 'suits' doing double duty in the surface as swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: When topless bathing is seen about town, standards are relaxed and nothing is forbidden.

clue.text: Meat-eater longing to tuck into pork cut

indicators.note: to tuck into means the longing word goes inside the meat
cut means the meat word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: ham is cured pork
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A carnivore with a craving tucks into a cut of pork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the meat's last letter, leaving HA, which then holds the longing.
explanation.definitionFit: This scavenging African animal is a carnivore, one that eats meat.

clue.text: Water fetchers' second tumbler

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme a pair go up the hill to fetch water; he falls first and she comes tumbling after

explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme she is the girl who comes tumbling after her companion falls down.

clue.text: Film's lead character is withdrawn philosopher

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: a film is a thin layer

explanation.surface: A movie's star walks off, leaving a philosophical question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it is a thin layer; losing its L gives the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher known for logical positivism.

clue.text: Young locust gardener gathers very quietly

indicators.note: gathers means the gardener holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a hoer is someone who works with a hoe
PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: A gardener quietly collects young locusts.
explanation.definitionFit: An immature locust that cannot yet fly is called this, from how it moves.

clue.text: Decline to perform about one year's worth of judgments

parts.note: to sag is to decline or droop

indicators.note: about means the perform word wraps the one

parts.note: to act is to perform
I is the Roman numeral for one
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A judge refuses to sit for another year, despite the value of their rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: This means wisdom and sound discernment, the quality that gives judgments their value.

clue.text: Rabbit, turning, goes after grass snake

indicators.note: goes after means the turned word follows the grass word

parts.note: to grass on someone is to inform, which is to rat

indicators.note: turning means the rabbit word is read backwards

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter, to gab

explanation.surface: A rabbit turns and chases after a grass snake.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on), from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk, is to gab; GAB turned is BAG. A grass is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake is a treacherous person, and this is an Australian and British term for a nasty one.

clue.text: Watch salesman scoff when fed properly

indicators.note: when fed means the scoff word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: to scoff is to jeer
properly means well

explanation.surface: A watch salesman scoffs his food when properly fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' suggests eating, but here it means mock.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling watches as well as gems and rings is run by this trader.
